summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of Crohn’s disease and multiple bowel resections was admitted for abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting concerning for partial small bowel obstruction. She presented with an NG tube in place from an outside hospital and elevated creatinine, likely due to dehydration. Imaging initially supported obstruction, but a follow-up abdominal X-ray on hospital day 4 showed resolution of bowel dilation. She was managed conservatively with bowel rest, IV fluids, and cautious pain control using IV Dilaudid within safe limits. A chest X-ray revealed a new right upper lobe consolidation suggestive of early pneumonia, though she remained asymptomatic and did not require antibiotics. She transitioned successfully to oral intake, had her NG tube removed, and was discharged on oral hydromorphone with plans for follow-up on pneumonia and GI issues. A flu vaccine was administered prior to discharge.
